findings: Launcher stores a small Intake ID to Codex session ID mapping under .agent-factory/runtime.
The actual Codex session is external to this mapping.
Lock files persist in the repository runtime path after process completion.
Intake canonical writes are already exclusively owned by intake.py.
interpretations: Session binding belongs with the named Intake but must be operational metadata that does not reopen readiness.
Locks should use an OS temporary runtime location.
